accepted.s: The Veerabhadra Swamy Temple at Lepakshi was built by which pair of Nayaka brothers?
accepted.x: The temple was built by the Nayaka brothers Virupanna and Veeranna of Penugonda. Virupanna was a governor or palegar.
accepted.tq: Test the builder through the APPSC favourite person–work association.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Lepakshi temple:
1. It was constructed in the c. 1530s.
2. Its construction is associated with the reign of Achyutaraya.
3. It was built on the banks of the Tungabhadra.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The temple belongs approximately to the 1530s and is associated with Achyutaraya's reign. The Tungabhadra location belongs to the Virupaksha temple at Hampi, not Lepakshi.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong location statement by separating Lepakshi facts from Hampi facts.

accepted.s: The Naga linga at Lepakshi is best described as:
o: A linga carved from a single boulder and sheltered by a seven-hooded serpent
A linga placed inside the stone chariot
A linga carved on the walls of the Ramachandra temple
A bronze linga installed by Krishnadevaraya
accepted.x: The Naga linga is carved from a single boulder and is sheltered by a seven-hooded serpent.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the distinctive physical feature from other Vijayanagara monuments.
accepted.sec: Lepakshi - builders, shrines, notable features, murals | Temples at Hampi - patron + popular name

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the technique of the Lepakshi murals?
o: Metallic pigments on granite with relief modelling
Oil colours on wooden panels with shaded naturalistic figures
Water colours on silk with miniature-style perspective
Mineral pigments on lime plaster with bold outlines, flat colour and elongated figures
accepted.x: The murals use mineral pigments such as ochre, green, black and white on lime plaster. Their style is marked by bold outlines, flat colours and elongated figures.
accepted.tq: Match the artistic medium and visual style rather than relying only on the subject matter.
accepted.sec: Lepakshi - builders, shrines, notable features, murals | Temples at Hampi - patron + popular name

accepted.s:
Which of the following subjects are represented in the Lepakshi murals?
1. Episodes from the Ramayana and Mahabharata
2. Parvati Parinayamu and Tripurasura Samharam
3. Shiva Tandavam, Bhikshatana and Dakshinamurti

accepted.x: The ceilings depict Ramayana and Mahabharata themes, while the walls contain Shiva-related subjects including Parvati Parinayamu, Tripurasura Samharam, Shiva Tandavam, Bhikshatana and Dakshinamurti.
accepted.tq: Recognise the all-inclusive thematic option after checking the separate mural subjects.

accepted.x: The Lepakshi murals are regarded as the finest or peak expression of the Vijayanagara school of painting.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Virupaksha Temple at Hampi is correct?
o: It was begun by Saluva Narasimha at Tirupati.
It is situated on the banks of the Krishna and was built entirely in the sixteenth century.
It is the first and largest temple of Hampi and stands on the bank of the Tungabhadra.
It was originally a royal-family temple dedicated to Bala Krishna.
accepted.x: Virupaksha is regarded as the first and largest temple of Hampi and is located on the Tungabhadra. It is associated with Shiva as Virupaksha or Pampapati.
accepted.tq: Use the precise location and status statement to reject swapped temple identities.
accepted.sec: Temples at Hampi - patron + popular name

accepted.s: The enlargement of the Virupaksha Temple at Hampi was undertaken by Lakkana Dandesha under:
accepted.x: Lakkana Dandesha enlarged the Virupaksha Temple under Devaraya II. The temple has older seventh-century origins.
accepted.tq: Apply the ruler–official–architectural work association.
accepted.sec: Temples at Hampi - patron + popular name

accepted.s:
With reference to the Virupaksha Temple, consider the following statements:
1. Krishnadevaraya added the central pillared hall.
2. Krishnadevaraya added the eastern gopuram.
3. The eastern gopuram was added in 1510.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Krishnadevaraya added both the central pillared hall and the eastern gopuram of the Virupaksha Temple; the gopuram was added in 1510.
accepted.tq: Check whether all closely connected date-and-builder statements belong to the same monument.
accepted.sec: Temples at Hampi - patron + popular name

accepted.s: The Hazara Rama Temple at Hampi was primarily associated with:
o: The royal family and the royal centre
The coronation of Saluva Narasimha at Tirupati
The worship of Narasimha at Ahobilam
accepted.x: The Hazara Rama or Ramachandra Temple was a royal-centre temple used by the royal family. Its walls contain Ramayana friezes.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional function of the monument rather than its popular name.
accepted.sec: Temples at Hampi - patron + popular name

accepted.s: Which architectural feature is specifically associated with the Hazara Rama Temple at Hampi?
o: A seven-hooded serpent over a monolithic linga
A stone chariot with musical pillars
accepted.x: The Hazara Rama Temple contains four Hoysala-style pillars and is noted for Ramayana friezes. The other features belong to Lepakshi or the Vitthala Temple.
accepted.tq: Separate similar Vijayanagara monuments by their distinctive architectural features.

accepted.s: The Vitthala Temple at Hampi is also known as:
accepted.x: The Vitthala Temple is popularly known as Saptaswara Devalayam, reflecting its association with musical pillars.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the popular names of the major Hampi temples.

Consider the following statements regarding the Vitthala Temple:

2. It is noted for musical pillars and a stone chariot.

accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Vitthala Temple is Vaishnava, contains musical pillars and a stone chariot, and was begun under Devaraya II and expanded by Krishnadevaraya.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the following temple–patron associations?
1. Mallikarjuna Temple at Srisailam — Mukha mandapam by Harihara II
2. Venkateswara Temple at Tirupati — Saluva Narasimha, followed by expansions under Krishnadevaraya and the Aravidus
3. Upper and Lower Narasimha Temples at Ahobilam — Early Vijayanagara rulers
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three associations are correct. Harihara II is associated with the mukha mandapam at Mallikarjuna, Saluva Narasimha with the initial Venkateswara patronage, and early Vijayanagara rulers with the Narasimha temples at Ahobilam.
accepted.tq: Combine three patron–temple pairs and reject any code containing a swapped patron.

Which of the following were associated with Krishnadevaraya's building activity at Hampi?

2. Hanuman statue
3. Monolithic Ganesha
